turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you again, Sandip, for your own good, not for the benefit of my tenantry, who have been bearing the brunt of your oppression.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You, my friend, are getting more and more pitiful. First, you warn me about the Mussulmans, and now you claim they're suffering under my oppression. I suppose you'd like to take credit for their suffering as well?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, for your own good, not to speak of the Mussulmans or my tenantry in the same breath. The suffering of my people is no concern of yours.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What an honour it is to be warned by you, Nikhil, about the Mussulmans. I'm sure your advice is as reliable as your arithmetic skills.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in this kind of petty banter with you, Sandip. My duty is to protect my tenantry, and I will not be swayed by your flippant remarks.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Really, Nikhil, you're so concerned about your tenantry's suffering, but what about the suffering of my poor crops due to the incessant rains? Are they too not worthy of your sympathy?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, to focus on your own lands and not spread your troubles to mine.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Why, Nikhil, you're as changeable as the wind, one moment warning me of the Mussulmans' wrath, the next lecturing me on the importance of focusing on my own lands. I suppose that's what they mean by 'statesmanlike' in the hallowed halls of your estate.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your jests, Sandip. The threat to my tenantry is real, and I will not ignore it. Bimala, tell Sandip that my warnings are not to be taken lightly.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Bimala, dear, please do enlighten me, my love. What exactly am I supposed to do with Nikhil's warnings? Am I to cower in fear, like a rabbit in the face of an oncoming storm?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: What is this threat Nikhil speaks of? Tell me, what evidence do you have for these claims?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have spoken to the village headman, and he has confirmed the Mussulmans' intentions to raid our lands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, the village headman, you say? I'm sure he's a font of unbiased wisdom, not at all influenced by your...let's call them 'generous' donations to his village.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I warn you again: do not underestimate the severity of this threat. The Mussulmans will not be swayed by your condescending remarks or your shallow attempts to curry favor with the villagers.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I think it would be wise to consider Nikhil's words, Sandip. Perhaps we should hear him out without dismissing his concerns.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not stand idly by while you mock the legitimate concerns of our villagers, Sandip. I demand that you take this threat seriously and prepare our defenses accordingly.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fancy that, Nikhil, you're suddenly concerned about the villagers' well-being. Perhaps it's not my condescending remarks that are shallow, but your attempts to manipulate them into your pocket.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps we can discuss the matter more calmly and rationally, without accusations and recriminations.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your petty jabs, Sandip. The safety of our people and our land is at stake, and I will not stand idly by while you dismiss the very real threat of the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the theatrics, Nikhil. You're as likely to be attacked by the Mussulmans as I am to grow a halo.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
